Senses.PreferredTarget: a general address to the community
Senses.Explanation: A general address is a scheduled public address to the monastic community, announced and staged as its own recorded-sayings event. Chan records give it a placard, venue, occasion, audience, and sometimes questions, making ordinary broad speaking an institution. The Classified Essentials of the Patriarchs lists “ascending the hall, small gathering, address to the assembly, and general address” (上堂、小參、示眾、普說) as separate headings. The monastic code makes its organization explicit: a general-address placard is hung before the monks' hall and common quarters, a venue is prepared, and the drum is sounded after gruel. Records qualify an address by occasion, as in an “incident-related general address” (因事普說), and record masters being requested to give one after questioning or before the summer retreat. Yuejian Shanquan says, “I will give you all one general address” (為諸人普說一上), while another request specifies the subject with “give a general address on this” (普說此). The ordinary wording is thus institutionalized as a placarded public recorded-sayings genre with venue, occasion, audience, and questioning. Event, heading, and delivery are grammatical presentations of the same institution, not different lexical things.
Senses.Note: Allowlist count: 870 hits in 134 texts. Noun and verb constructions denote the same general-address event; the two former targets could not distinguish different referents without their explanations and are merged. The general-address placard (普說牌) names the placard for this genre, not another sense. General address remains distinct from ascending the hall (上堂), small gathering (小參), addressing the assembly (示眾), question-and-answer, and taking up the whisk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 侍者出寢堂，候眾集入，請住持出據坐。普說與小參禮同。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X63/X63n1250.xml). Chan Grove Ready-Reference Pure Regulations (禪林備用清規). This monastic-rule passage prescribes the rite of the general address (普說): the attendant comes out of the hall, waits for the community to gather, and requests the abbot to take the seat, and the rite is shared with the small assembly (小參). Compiled by Yixian as procedural text, it names no speaking master.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: X63n1250 0628d04-05: the passage 侍者出寢堂，候眾集入，請住持出據坐。普說與小參禮同。 is procedural rule text of the Chan Grove Ready-Reference Pure Regulations compiled by Yixian; the line, the expanded context, the section header (普說), the book title, the TEI header, and exact and parallel searches name no speaking master — the general address is prescribed, not uttered — so the occurrence stays impersonal monastic-rule procedural text.
